design_rationale: The study randomized preschool teachers and their classrooms to either the shared book reading intervention or a business-as-usual comparison condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although random assignment of teachers/classes was performed, the sequence generation and allocation concealment details were not described, and post-randomization dropouts (6 teachers) occurred before implementation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomly selected 24 teachers to implement the interactive content-enriched shared book reading curricular intervention and 24 for the comparison condition referred to as business-as-usual (BAU). Six teachers withdrew before the intervention began... reducing our total number to 42 teacher participants (treatment, n = 23; BAU, n = 19).

domain_judgments.rationale: Interventions were delivered as intended in classroom contexts, fidelity was monitored systematically, and an appropriate multilevel analysis accounting for clustering was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All instruction (content-enriched intervention and BAU) occurred during teachers' regularly scheduled book reading time... Teachers were told to read their book of choice to the small group of six students for approximately 20 min a day for the 18-week scheduled period.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was very low across both standardized and researcher-developed measures (over 92% of randomized children had complete posttest data) and non-completers did not differ significantly on demographic characteristics.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to missing data, we further examined any potential differences between completers (i.e., 249 children on PPVT-4; 238 children on EVT-2) and non-completers (i.e., 3 children on PPVT-4; 14 children on EVT-2) on the demographic variables. No statistically significant differences were found...

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessments included subjective/examiner-scored expressive measures (RDEPVT scored 0-2), and there is no statement confirming whether data collectors were blinded to classroom intervention status.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All student participants were individually administered the battery of English vocabulary assessments by trained bilingual (Spanish/English) graduate research assistants/assessors (n = 6)... All bilingual data collectors participated in a 2-day training with practice opportunities before pre- and post-test data collection and were required to demonstrate 100% mastery on all measures prior to each testing interval.

domain_judgments.rationale: No formal pre-registration or published analysis protocol was referenced, though results for all four planned vocabulary measures were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We then estimated four two-level models, one for each posttest outcome measure (i.e., PPVT-4 standard scores, EVT-2 standard scores, RDRPVT, and RDEPVT raw scores).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as 'some concerns' due to insufficient reporting of allocation sequence generation and concealment, lack of explicit confirmation of outcome assessor blinding on researcher-developed expressive measures, and the absence of a pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which bilingual children were randomly assigned to monolingual treatment, bilingual treatment, or delayed-treatment control groups using an online random number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although a random sequence was generated and sealed envelopes were used, one participant was non-randomly allocated to the control group due to scheduling issues, and there was a baseline difference on one test (EOWPVT).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random assignment was accomplished using the “Research Randomizer” website (http://www.randomizer.org), generating six sets of six numbers per set... The order of randomization was kept in sealed numbered envelopes... No change was made from the randomly assigned condition for any participant, with one exception involving a child for whom it became apparent immediately after the intake that his family needed to go away on an extended trip, which would have made intervention impossible at that point. This participant was selected to serve as a delayed-treatment control without random assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel delivering behavioral intervention was not feasible, and participants who withdrew post-randomization were excluded from analysis rather than analyzed according to an intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In both conditions, one of the child’s parents attended all therapy sessions, and those in the bilingual condition participated directly... In addition, five children who qualified for the intervention phase withdrew from the study... The remaining three children withdrew after two, three, and six intervention sessions, respectively. Two had been assigned to bilingual treatment and one to monolingual treatment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Five of 34 eligible/allocated children withdrew and were excluded from primary analyses, and secondary L1 spontaneous language sample outcomes were missing for substantial portions of each group (only 21 of 29 completed).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants who completed the study included 29 children... In addition, five children who qualified for the intervention phase withdrew from the study... Every effort was made to secure interpreters to record and transcribe L1 spontaneous language samples for each child, resulting in completion of such samples for 21 children at pre- and posttest: eight in the MT group, eight in the BT group, and five in the NT group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and scorers were blinded to the treatment condition, and standardized or clearly specified objective scoring probes were used across all groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Language evaluations were conducted before and after treatment by blinded examiners; these evaluations targeted French as well as the home languages... Posttreatment assessment and scoring were done by research assistants blinded to the children’s treatment conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registration or published prospective trial analysis plan was referenced, leaving some concerns regarding potential flexibility in outcome reporting and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The vocabulary and story retell probes assess skills directly targeted in therapy and, therefore, are expected to be more sensitive to treatment effects than more general language tests or spontaneous language. These are the main outcome measures of this study, although pre- and postscores are also reported for other language measures.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to be of some concerns due to minor deviations from pure random assignment for one participant, non-intention-to-treat analysis following post-randomization dropouts, and the absence of a prospective trial registration analysis protocol.

design_rationale: Participants were individual children randomly assigned to either an intervention or a business-as-usual control group in an RCT.

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states participants were randomized at an individual level, but details of sequence generation and allocation concealment are not described, although baseline characteristics were well-balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The children were randomized on an individual level to a treatment or a control condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention fidelity was actively monitored and high (90% implementation rate), contamination was addressed by explicit instructions, and analysis adhered to an intention-to-treat approach using full information maximum likelihood.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The participating children were located in fifty-five different classrooms. Among these, fourteen classes ended up having both children receiving the intervention and children distributed to the control group. In these cases, preferably, the teachers from other classes were responsible for the intervention. If this was not possible, to avoid problems related to treatment diffusion, the teachers who participated in the intervention had thorough instructions about the dangers of diffusion.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 2 out of 115 children (one per group) were lost to follow-up due to relocation, meaning attrition was negligible (under 2%) and balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Lost to follow-up due to relocation (n =1) [in each group]

domain_judgments.rationale: It is not reported whether the research assistants conducting the oral language and vocabulary assessments were blinded to group allocation, introducing potential detection bias for tests involving subjective scoring.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All testing was performed individually in Norwegian with each child. Trained research assistants performed the testing, and the tests were administered in a fixed order.

domain_judgments.rationale: No formal pre-registration or prospective statistical analysis plan was cited, leaving some concern regarding potential flexibility in modeling decisions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analyses of effects were performed with Mplus, version 7.3 (Muthen & Muthen, 1998-2014), using latent autoregressive models (Structural Equation Models) with maximum-likelihood estimation to handle missing data.

overall_summary: The trial is well conducted with minimal attrition and monitored fidelity, but some concerns exist regarding unreported sequence generation/concealment mechanisms, lack of explicit assessor blinding, and absence of a pre-registered analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study employed a cluster-randomized design where elementary schools (units) were randomly assigned to either the experimental (enhanced practice) or control (typical practice) condition.

domain_judgments.rationale: While schools were randomly assigned, the exact sequence generation and concealment were not specified, 5 schools were dropped post-randomization, and baseline oral English proficiency differed substantially between groups (e.g., SEI-T vs SEI-E).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random assignment was performed among the 28 elementary schools in the district meeting these criteria. Because we encountered a low return rate of parental consent forms at some schools and fewer students enrolled in SEI at some of the schools than initially anticipated, we were forced to eliminate 5 schools... Hence, this project was a quasi-experimental design at the student level and an experimental design at the school level.

domain_judgments.rationale: The analysis excluded participants who did not remain continuously enrolled in their assigned track across all three assessment rounds (per-protocol rather than intention-to-treat approach), and teachers naturally could not be blinded to the extensive instructional intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: To augment the sample size, another 100 kindergarten students who were enrolled in the randomly assigned schools were added in the fall of 2004... In the present analyses, only those who participated in all three rounds of assessments were included. These students had been enrolled continuously and remained in the same program as their initial placement since kindergarten through the end of first grade.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial attrition occurred due to a reported student mobility rate of nearly 35% and exclusion of anyone lacking complete longitudinal data across all three time points, creating a high risk of attrition bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the present analyses, only those who participated in all three rounds of assessments were included... The total number of students who met this designated criterion was 534... we were not able to study the least stable part of the student population because of a high mobility rate (nearly 35%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Standardized tests (WLPB-R subtests) were used, but there is no mention that the outcome assessors (testers and paraprofessionals who also delivered interventions) were blinded to the intervention assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both of the tests were administered individually outside the classroom to minimize distraction, and the testers were well trained... All paraprofessionals were trained in interventions biweekly, and they, along with the testers, were trained and had to pass the proficiency test for giving assessments as established by the research team.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered protocol or analysis plan was referenced, and the primary outcome analysis utilized a post-hoc constructed composite score to reduce model complexity.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, to reduce the complexity of the model, we computed a composite score as an observed variable for each time point. Raw data were converted into percentage scores (a ratio between the number of items answered correct and the total number of items in the test), and the two percentage scores collected at the same time were averaged as a composite score indicating oral proficiency at each time point.

overall_summary: The study has an overall high risk of bias driven predominantly by substantial missing outcome data (approximately 35% attrition due to high student mobility and complete-case restriction), along with post-randomization school exclusions, unblinded assessors who included intervention delivery personnel, and lack of pre-registration.

design_rationale: Children were randomly assigned to one of three conditions (control, English-only intervention, or transitional intervention).

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper states that children were randomly assigned to conditions, but details regarding sequence generation and allocation concealment are omitted, and baseline values show some differences across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Ninety-four children were randomly assigned either to a control condition (HighScope Preschool Curriculum) or to receive small-group pull-out instruction (Literacy Express Preschool Curriculum) in English or initially in Spanish and transitioning to English.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention fidelity and attendance were high and monitored, and deviations from intended interventions were minimal.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Children in both the English-only and the transitional conditions were present for 86% of all sessions. Children in the control condition had an attendance rate of 87%. Each week, interventionists' small-group sessions were observed and rated by the intervention supervisor using a 5-point scale of fidelity of implementation (e.g., activities conducted in prescribed manner, content of session, pacing; 1 = low fidelity, 5 = high fidelity). Across interventionists, 90%–98% of the rated sessions received a score of 5, indicating that the intervention was provided to children as intended.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data appear complete for all 94 randomized participants across pretest and posttest descriptive tables, with contrast analyses including the expected sample sizes (N = 63 for each pairwise comparison with control).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Note. N = 94. Adjusted M = scores adjusted for chronological age. Min = minimum; max = maximum. ... Note. N = 63.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed using standardized, validated measures by trained research assistants who were masked to intervention condition.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The assessments were administered by bilingual graduate and undergraduate research assistants who were trained in the administration of the P-CTOPPP. These research assistants were not involved in the implementation of the intervention, and they had no knowledge of the intervention conditions to which children were assigned.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no indication of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan for the secondary moderation analyses, creating some risk of selective analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In these analyses, multiple regression models were conducted with three steps. For the analyses examining L1 to L2 transfer, the first step included the main effect of intervention condition as well as both L1 and L2 pretest skills. In the second step, an Intervention Condition × Initial L1 Skill interaction term was added to the models. In the third step, an Intervention Condition × Initial L2 Skill interaction term was added to the models.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as 'some concerns' due to insufficient reporting of the random sequence generation and allocation concealment methods, along with the lack of a pre-registered statistical analysis plan for the complex moderation models.

design_rationale: The study is a cluster-randomized controlled trial where 31 classes from 12 kindergartens were randomly assigned to treatment or control groups using a blocked randomization procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although classes were randomly assigned using blocking factors and baseline characteristics were balanced, the authors do not describe the specific method used to generate the random allocation sequence or whether allocation concealment was maintained prior to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: instead of complete randomization, we used a blocked randomization process at the class level, blocked by city, the kindergarten ranking, and children’s entry age cohort... There were no signiﬁcant differences in children’s ages, genders, or Uyghur or Chinese vocabulary scores between the treatment and control group at the beginning of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention fidelity was actively monitored and high, contamination was evaluated and ruled out, and the multilevel growth modeling analysis included all participants across time points without inappropriate exclusions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The staff also visited control group classes every three weeks to check if their teaching approaches were affected by the interventions in the neighboring classrooms. The observation reports suggested no evidence of contamination. The control group did not use any of the material provided to the treatment group. The teachers of treatment group reported that they were able to complete 82–90% of the curriculum plan.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was low (17 out of 256 children, ~6.6%) due to family relocation, and sensitivity analysis using multiple imputation yielded consistent results with the primary individual growth models.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, we lost seventeen children in the second and third waves of tests. We ran the analysis with multiple imputations (Rubin, 2004) and found that the results of the XJP efﬁcacy were consistent with the ﬁndings of models without imputed data (results available from authors).

domain_judgments.rationale: Standardized and adapted vocabulary tests were administered individually by trained assessors who were explicitly blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Prior to data collection, testers received training via workshops and practiced testing with children ages 4–6 from schools outside of the study. The testers were blind to treatment and control conditions.

domain_judgments.rationale: No formal pre-registration or prospective analysis plan is referenced, leaving some concerns regarding potential flexibility in model selection and reporting across multiple outcomes and interaction terms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used an individual growth modeling framework employing generalized linear mixed models and found that the intervention led to a more rapid development of Chinese receptive vocabulary (effect size = 0.68) and Uyghur expressive vocabulary (effect size = 0.38).

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to insufficient details regarding sequence generation and allocation concealment in the randomization process (Domain 1) as well as the lack of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan (Domain 5). Other domains (deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and measurement of the outcome) were assessed at low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study used a cluster-randomized design in which 25 preschool classrooms were randomly assigned to treatment (12 classrooms) and control (13 classrooms) groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Classrooms were randomly assigned, but details regarding the random sequence generation and allocation concealment were not reported, raising some concerns.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 25 classrooms were included in this study. The classrooms were randomly assigned to treatment and control groups at the completion of the consenting and screening process, resulting in 12 classrooms in the treatment group and 13 in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Teachers and participants could not be blinded to classroom assignment, and substantial implementation deviations occurred (e.g., three classrooms lacked Spanish-speaking staff and 10 of 43 treatment children did not receive Tier 2 small-group instruction as intended), though an intention-to-treat analysis across all consented participants was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In five of the 12 treatment classrooms, more than three children qualified to be research participants... only three children in each class were able to receive the intended multitiered instruction, and the rest of the children (n = 10) received only large-group instruction in English. The teachers determined which children would receive the smallgroup instruction, and the researchers did not guide them in making those choices. Although 10 of the 43 children who were identified as needing Tier 2 small-group support only received large-group instruction, these 10 children were included as research participants because they received part of the intended intervention and the control group received none of it.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data were minimal (less than 1% overall), making bias due to missing data unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Less than 1% of the scores were missing overall (18/2754 = 0.0065, or 0.65%), and all available data were used in the multilevel model results that follow.

domain_judgments.rationale: Assessors who administered and scored the subjective oral language assessments (including real-time narrative retell and open-ended story comprehension questions) were unblinded to group condition, introducing high risk of measurement bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because they were all needed to observe fidelity, support teachers delivery of the intervention, and collect data, they were not blind to assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified analysis plan, and scoring decisions (such as retaining the highest score among multiple forms) were not shown to be pre-specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Because NLM Listening stories are similar to those directly taught in Puente de Cuentos, this was considered a proximal outcome measure for this study. ... At each assessment time point, the children were administered three of the NLM Listening parallel forms in a single session lasting 3 to 4 minutes. However, only the retell with the highest score was used in the analysis and to identify the participants.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by unblinded outcome assessors administering and scoring subjective oral language measures (e.g., real-time narrative retell and open-ended comprehension questions). Additionally, there were some concerns regarding allocation concealment and potential selective outcome reporting.
